comparator.name: Data Science for Global Challenges
comparator.sourceNotes: Current2026–2027 BDS handbook replaces the historical2025PDF schemes:111EC compulsory common courses,3EC preparation-dependent mathematics/statistics,6EC restricted choice and24EC individual integrated thesis=144commonEC. Select first listed BayesianDataAnalysis from the either/or choice with DecisionScience1;36genuine elective/minor credits close180. Completing57B1common+3choice=60B1 and54B2common+6restricted=60B2 leaves24thesis+36electives=60B3. The old12ECthesis/3ECpreparation/15ECgroupchallenge cluster is not current. Thesis requires102BDScredits including all60B1, approved topic and supervisors covering both data science and the application domain, and four months full-time individual research with proposal/data analysis/report/presentation/defence. General programme is available in Dutch or English; normalized Dutch registry identity is not changed and no academic track is selected merely for the output language. Current exact module AK assumptions are distinguished from hard requirements; obsolete advisory codes do not create an extra unsupported cohort gate when current programme/competencies are explicit.
components: WUR begins integrated group research across agri-food, health and environment. UCR’s selected domain and data courses provide substantive ingredients, but do not guarantee the same coordinated research cycle.

UCR Earth Observation supplies direct GIS, remote-sensing, projections, spatial queries and image-processing methods in the environmental programme. The other illustrated UCR programmes have less dedicated geospatial training.

WUR students conduct further integrated domain-data projects, including data management, interdisciplinary collaboration and communication. Separate UCR domain projects are not a substitute for this fixed data-science integration course.

Both develop advanced programming and software construction. WUR uses Python, graphical interfaces and data-source integration; UCR Software Development uses C++ and Haskell, with software design, testing and code review.

UCR supplies biological/genetic mechanisms and, in the health programme, introductory molecular database/laboratory work. WUR has a dedicated practical bioinformatics course; that specialist tools sequence remains a gap.
Introduction to Epidemiology and Public Health
Relational database design, SQL and normalisation are shared. WUR additionally develops RDF, ontologies, SPARQL and linked-data/knowledge-graph approaches.
WUR includes distributed big-data architectures, MapReduce and scalable analysis platforms. The selected UCR data, database and machine-learning courses do not reproduce that dedicated sequence.

Neural Networks & Deep Learning includes text classification/generation and transformers. WUR provides a dedicated language-processing course with linguistic representations, language models and domain applications.

Ethics, privacy, fairness, responsibility and social effects are shared. WUR adds explicit ethical/legal/social redesign through its ELSA lab and domain cases; UCR’s projects use broader psychological and ethical contexts.

Image filtering, segmentation, recognition pipelines and performance evaluation are shared. WUR applies machine vision to agricultural tasks and also covers spectral images and 3D point clouds; UCR applications and scope differ.
This example uses Mathematics Applied: Introduction for VWO Mathematics A. Students with Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead; the choice follows prior preparation.
This example selects Bayesian Data Analysis from the restricted choice with Decision Science 1. It builds on advanced statistics and working knowledge of R; the alternative is not added here.
BSc Thesis Data Science for Global Challenges

WUR requires a 24 EC individual thesis integrating data science and a life-science domain. Entry requires at least 102 bachelor credits, including all 60 first-year credits. The programme must approve the topic and supervisors; supervision must cover both data science and the domain. Optional UCR 15 EC independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 EC.
With one 6 EC restricted option selected, this pathway retains 36 EC for a minor and/or individually chosen electives. No specific minor is invented.

core: Programming, algorithms, data management, AI, machine learning, language and vision methods
Life-science domain knowledge and global-challenge applications in agri-food, health and environment
Mathematics, statistics, Bayesian inference, quantitative modelling and research data
Responsible interdisciplinary integration, stakeholder communication and individual research
adjacent: Environmental data science, satellite/sensor information and geospatial/climate inquiry
questions: How can computational and statistical methods turn domain data into useful scientific evidence?
How can data illuminate climate, environmental and food-system problems?
How can data science be used responsibly in health and other life-science domains?

candidates.label: Data science for health & molecular systems

alternatives.label: Data science, life sciences & sustainable systems
alternatives.labelReason: Combine programming, data management, algorithms, statistical inference, machine learning, vision and responsible AI with cell/genetic biology, epidemiology, ecological models and farming/environmental assessment. Build the technical and domain understanding needed to interpret data across health, agri-food and environment, while recognising the absence of WUR’s fixed integrated projects and individual data-science thesis.
alternatives.concept: Combine programming, data management, algorithms, statistical inference, machine learning, vision and responsible AI with cell/genetic biology, epidemiology, ecological models and farming/environmental assessment. Build the technical and domain understanding needed to interpret data across health, agri-food and environment, while recognising the absence of WUR’s fixed integrated projects and individual data-science thesis.
progression: Every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier term and every scheduled offering is planned in the fixed Fall2026 cohort. Mathematical Methods precedes LinearAlgebra/Probability/NumericalMethods, Python precedes dependent programming/algorithms/AI, empirical statistics precedes ML and cell biology precedes molecular pathology/genetics. Actual scientific/domain progression and course evidence were considered; no old offerings restored.

alternatives.label: Environmental data science & geospatial analysis
alternatives.labelReason: Apply a sustained data-science and AI foundation to environmental questions through GIS/remote sensing, Earth-system tools, climate science, geochemical modelling and ecological/farming sustainability. Combine actual geospatial and quantitative methods with stakeholder-facing sustainability appraisal, without promising a specific satellite, sensor or partner dataset in every course.

trace: Direct Python structured programming, data collections, recursion, testing and debugging supply actual data-science programming foundations; no domain-specific project guaranteed in this gateway.

Biomolecules, cells, energy metabolism, DNA/heredity, gene expression and experiment/literature appraisal supply actual life-science domain understanding for interpreting biological data; not wet-lab or specialist bioinformatics training.

Direct disease-frequency/risk measures, study design, bias/confounding/causality, outbreak analysis and population-health data appraisal provide a real epidemiological domain/method contribution. Disease-spread modelling is not assumed to mean a taught compartment-model course.

Actual organism/phylogenetic diversity, species identification, biodiversity indices and data collection/analysis supply concrete ecological measurement and domain interpretation, relevant to environmental monitoring and farming impacts.

Calculus, optimisation, differential equations and dynamic-model implementation supply quantitative foundations for model behaviour, learning and biological/ecological systems. Its detailed current content is not the separate linear-algebra course.

Actual R cleaning, joins, exploration, visualisation and tabular/text/spatial data work implement central data-science concepts. Choice of project data is open, not guaranteed agri-food/clinical/climate work.

Ethical theory, fairness/privacy/accountability, human–AI interaction and psychological/social effects support responsible data science. Actual framework-based projects/podcasts do not reproduce WUR’s domain ELSA redesign lab or a legal qualification.
Direct vectors/matrices, eigenvalues, orthogonality, least squares, SVD and PCA supply substantial computational/statistical modelling foundations, with analytical and computer-algebra work.

Direct multivariable regression, ANOVA/ANCOVA, categorical/repeated-measures models, assumption diagnostics and R analyses support empirical data-science study design. The applications are behavioural/health rather than all global-challenge domains.

Actual data structures, sorting/searching, string/graph algorithms, asymptotic analysis and experimental benchmarking supply substantial computational problem-solving and performance methods; application contexts differ from life-science-specific data conventions.

Actual product/process life-cycle assessment, environmental/social/health impacts, circular-resource use and cost/revenue appraisal supply substantive systems-based domain measures. No particular food-chain or computational dataset is promised.

The available course description fully supports relational database theory, SQL, authorisation, normalisation and query processing. These are substantive data-management methods; RDF/SPARQL, knowledge graphs and distributed big-data systems are not inferred.

Direct cellular organisation, membranes, signalling, trafficking, gene expression and reproducibility/method appraisal supply a substantial biological mechanisms foundation for data interpretation and model/domain questions.

Actual ecological population dynamics, competition/predation/food webs and energy/matter models, including R ecological modelling and a research project, supply real environmental quantitative mechanisms and data interpretation.

Actual C++/Haskell program construction, object-oriented/functional abstractions, version control, code review, debugging/testing and documentation strengthen reliable scientific software. The course does not teach WUR’s Python GUI/data-source integration sequence.

Probability, estimation/testing, Bayesian reasoning and MonteCarlo/Gibbs sampling provide substantial uncertainty/inference methods for scientific data. WUR BayesianDataAnalysis develops a more specialised applied Bayesian modelling course.

Direct regression/classification, resampling/validation, regularisation, trees, dimension reduction and model evaluation in R/Python implement substantial machine-learning substance, with actual held-out predictive work.

Bayesian/temporal networks, probabilistic inference, expected utility, Markov decision processes and multi-agent reasoning supply substantive AI-agent and uncertainty methods. They are not a full ML/vision or domain-integration sequence.

Actual inheritance/variation, gene regulation, molecular diagnosis, cellular pathology and genetic technologies make biological/health datasets interpretable; research-grant design supplies hypothesis/control/feasibility reasoning. It is not a dedicated sequence-analysis bioinformatics course.

Actual Python/Keras/TensorFlow neural networks, training/regularisation, text classification/generation and transformers implement substantial deep-learning/NLP methods. Image-or-text project choice is explicit; no dedicated biological language dataset is promised.

Direct Python/OpenCV filtering, segmentation, feature detection/tracking, recognition-pipeline construction and unseen-image benchmarking implement substantive computer-vision methods. Spectral/3D agricultural sensing and particular medical/satellite datasets are not guaranteed.

Actual environmental appraisal of agriculture, animal husbandry/aquaculture, farming innovation and alternative proteins supplies substantive agri-food domain knowledge; comparative scientific-literature research informs data/model questions without promising an integrated data-science project.

Institutions, stakeholder power, food/water/energy governance, public goods/externalities and policy-option analysis give actual tools for interpreting domain needs and communicating responsible solutions. The Zeeland stakeholder project is not guaranteed a data-science application.

Chemical/thermodynamic principles, environmental dynamic models and graph/uncertainty reasoning supply the scientific foundations required by the selected Earth-analysis courses. Actual material experiment is not a remote-sensing data lab.

Actual greenhouse gases, feedbacks/tipping points, ocean/sea-level/ecological/agricultural impacts and mitigation/adaptation mechanisms supply climate domain knowledge for responsible data interpretation; stakeholder/film work is not climate-model programming.

Actual aqueous chemistry, carbonate/redox/mineral processes, geochemical equilibrium/speciation modelling, laboratory data and environmental case work provide mechanisms and model-validation context for environmental data. It is not generic sustainability breadth.

Direct ArcGIS geospatial data models/projections, queries/transformations, surface analysis, remote-sensing acquisition/preprocessing and image processing supply actual satellite/drone environmental data methods and a collaborative case study.

Available description supports Earth-system interactions/modelling, proxies/isotope tracers and climate interpretation with a greenhouse-gas field trip. Give these substantive domain/method contributions full consideration; no undocumented software, geospatial technique or calibration routine is inferred.

Actual homeostasis, endocrine/nervous and organ-system regulation, metabolism and reproduction supply human physiological mechanisms for interpreting health data/models; the course’s literature paper is not a clinical prediction project.

Actual biomolecular structure, enzymes/kinetics and carbohydrate/lipid/nitrogen energy pathways supply biochemical mechanisms for molecular-health data. Disease literature connects mechanism to observations, not a guaranteed omics analysis.

Actual microbial/protein/DNA methods, ELISA/PCR, electrophoresis and introductory biological database interpretation provide concrete experimental-data literacy and reproducibility. Introductory database use is not the complete WUR bioinformatics tool sequence.

Actual numerical root finding, interpolation, differential-equation/system solvers and validation of error/stability/convergence provide concrete scientific-computing methods for health/biological modelling. It is not just an additional mathematics label.

Actual immune/host-pathogen mechanisms, vaccination and original flow-cytometry-data analysis supply substantial infection/immune domain and measurement knowledge. It is not a clinical AI deployment course.

Actual organ-system pathophysiology, clinical-case/diagnostic evidence appraisal and mechanistic explanation supply concrete health-domain constraints on interpreting or proposing models; no clinical qualification or guaranteed health dataset is implied.
blocks: Programming, data systems, AI & quantitative methods
Shared Python programming, control flow, functions, data collections and computational problem-solving. Specific libraries, projects and application contexts differ.

Shared advanced program construction, object-oriented abstractions, software design and quality work. WUR uses Python GUI/data-source applications; UCR uses C++/Haskell with testing/version control/code review.
Shared data structures, accompanying algorithms, performance analysis and computational implementation. WUR foregrounds food/health/environment data conventions and stakeholder communication.
Shared relational design, normalisation, SQL and query processing. WUR additionally teaches RDF, ontologies, SPARQL and linked/knowledge-graph data.

Shared data acquisition/manipulation, cleaning, exploration, visualisation and analysis workflow. WUR explicitly integrates domain project blocks and broader governance/cloud concepts; UCR includes R text/spatial data work.

Shared supervised/unsupervised learning, regression/classification, validation, regularisation, clustering/dimension reduction and performance appraisal. WUR domain projects explicitly connect biosystems, GIS or bioinformatics.

Shared neural text classification/generation, transformers and language-model foundations. WUR has a dedicated NLP sequence, linguistic representations and domain projects with broader contemporary language-model design/evaluation.

Shared image acquisition/representation, filtering, segmentation, detection, recognition pipelines and performance evaluation. WUR adds agricultural machine-control cases, spectral images and3Dpoints.

Shared intelligent-agent decision foundations, uncertainty and probabilistic reasoning. WUR additionally integrates supervised/unsupervised/reinforcement methods and hands-on life-science AI projects.
Shared functions, calculus, differential equations and analytical/computational modelling. UCR extends into dynamic models and numerical tools; the conditional preparation module remains separate.
Shared vectors, matrices, linear systems, eigenvalues, projections/regression and mathematical software, with broader vector-space/SVD/PCA development at UCR.

Shared Bayesian updating/uncertainty, statistical inference and MonteCarlo/Gibbs sampling. WUR develops dedicated applied Bayesian modelling withR; UCR is broader probability/mathematical statistics withMathematica.
Shared multivariable regression, ANOVA/ANCOVA, categorical/repeated-measures models, assumptions and R-based statistical interpretation.
The separate basic applied-inference/regression award remains distinct; the strongest UCR empirical-statistics course is aligned to AdvancedStatistics, not duplicated.
Biological mechanisms and introductory molecular database literacy do not reproduce the dedicated practical bioinformatics tools/analysis sequence.
No selected dedicated distributed big-data architecture, MapReduce and scalable-platform course. Ordinary data/database/ML work is not substituted for this.
Conditional prior-preparation introduction remains separate; UCR MathematicalMethods is aligned once to the stronger applied-analysis component.
Life sciences, health, environment & global challenges
Shared cell organisation, membranes, signalling, gene expression and cellular mechanisms. WUR includes its own cell/biochemical practicals; UCR develops molecular mechanisms and research appraisal.
Shared epidemiological measures, designs, bias/confounding, causality and population-health reasoning; UCR adds local needs/stakeholder appraisal.
Shared GIS data models, geo-reference/projections, spatial queries/transformations, remote-sensing foundations, image processing and applied geospatial work.
Shared ethical frameworks, fairness/privacy, responsibility and social implications of data/AI. WUR adds explicit legal/social ELSA redesign methodology and domain cases.
Separate domain/data courses do not reproduce the prescribed integrated agri-food/health/environment group research cycle and bridge-building training.
No selected UCR course guarantees the specific second integrated data-science project, FAIR/ELSA domain-data management and coordinated interdisciplinary research cycle.

Required24ECindividual domain-integrated data-science research, proposal, analyses, report, presentation and defence have no taught-course equivalent. OptionalUCR15ECindependentresearch is an additional opportunity outside24courses/180EC.
Genuine36EC minor/elective space has no specified subject counterpart.

selection.assessment: Three sequentially tested material data-science responses combine sustained computation/statistics with actual life-science or environmental knowledge. All16eligible generators are owned once. The old business/media-heavy domain labels and empty-generator methods candidate are superseded; curriculum-method topics do not create an additional programme. The fixed WUR integration, specialist big-data/bioinformatics and individual thesis differences remain explicit.

notes.text: The UCR programmes combine substantial computing, statistics and AI with actual biological or environmental study. WUR prescribes more coordinated data-science/domain projects, specialist bioinformatics and distributed big-data training, and an individual 24 EC thesis with approved cross-domain supervision. UCR’s optional 15 EC independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 EC; it does not reproduce that required thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: WUR’s Data Science for Global Challenges bachelor combines computing, statistics and AI with agri-food, health and environmental knowledge. Students learn to connect domain questions with data, interpret evidence responsibly and conduct integrated research. The programme is available in Dutch or English.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme combines a sustained data-science foundation with biological, epidemiological, ecological and farming/systems study. The second emphasises environmental data and geospatial methods; the third emphasises health and molecular mechanisms. Each retains substantial programming, statistics, machine learning and responsible AI. WUR adds its fixed integrated domain-data projects, specialist bioinformatics/big-data work and required 24 EC individual thesis; UCR’s optional independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 credits.
